transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I feel like I’m falling apart. Ever since the foreclosure notices started coming, I’ve been crying in my truck before work, jumping every time the phone rings, snapping at the apprentices… and I’m making dumb mistakes in the repair bay that I never used to make. I don’t feel like myself.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge most of the time since you started getting the foreclosure notices?

Yes. Since those notices started coming, I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. I’m on edge all the time—crying in my truck before work, jumping when the phone rings, snapping at the apprentices. And I’m making stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since you started getting the foreclosure notices?

Yes. Since the foreclosure notices started, I’ve been crying in my truck before work and just feeling like I’m falling apart. It’s not like me. I’m sad most of the time, and it comes out at work too—I’m short with people and making mistakes I normally wouldn’t make.
Do you still enjoy activities or hobbies that you used to find pleasurable?

Not really. I used to keep up with church volunteering, fitness classes, and truck-club outings, but I’ve pretty much stopped showing up. And at work, they’ve taken me out of the high-risk repair bay, so even the stuff I used to take pride in feels out of reach right now.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

Yeah… it feels like that. I mean, the things that used to make me feel good or normal—I’ve stopped going to church volunteering, fitness classes, and the truck-club outings. And at work, being taken out of the high-risk repair bay… that really hit me. Those things used to matter to me, and now I just can’t seem to get anything out of them.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not much, honestly. I’ve pretty much stopped going to the church volunteering, the fitness classes, and the truck-club stuff I used to keep up with. And at work, being pulled out of the high-risk repair bay has taken away one of the few things I used to feel good about.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes. I’ve lost interest in a lot of it. I don’t show up for the church volunteering, fitness classes, or the truck-club outings anymore like I used to. And at work, being taken out of the high-risk repair bay… that’s been hard, because that was something I used to care about.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since you started getting the foreclosure notices?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking my weight, and I can’t say I’ve noticed a major change one way or the other.
Do you feel guilty or worthless about your current situation?
I don’t know if I’d call it worthless. I do feel bad about it, and I blame myself some days, like I should’ve handled things better. But I’m not sure it’s guilt exactly.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself since you started getting the foreclosure notices?
I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I’ve been really overwhelmed, but I don’t think I can say more than that right now.
Have you had any thoughts of death or dying since you started getting the foreclosure notices?
I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve been scared and stressed about everything, but I’m not sure I’ve been thinking about death exactly. It’s hard to put into words.
Have you been having any flashbacks or nightmares related to the foreclosure notices or your current situation?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have a hard time sleeping sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it nightmares or flashbacks. I don’t feel like I’m reliving anything like that.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future, like what will happen with your home or your job?

Yes. Ever since those foreclosure notices started coming, I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. I worry all the time about what’s going to happen, and it’s affecting me at work too—crying in my truck before I go in, jumping every time the phone rings, snapping at the apprentices. I’ve even been making stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before.
How long have you been feeling this way since the foreclosure notices started?
About four months now. It pretty much started when the foreclosure notices started coming in, and it hasn’t really let up since.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions since the foreclosure notices started?

Yes. I’m having a hard time keeping my head straight. At work I’m making stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before, and I catch myself just freezing up over simple things. Since those notices started coming, I feel like I’m coming apart at the seams.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities because they remind you of your financial situation or the foreclosure notices?

I don’t know that I’m avoiding places or people because of it. I mean, I don’t like dealing with anything that has to do with the foreclosure, but I haven’t really noticed myself staying away from certain people or activities for that reason.
Have you been avoiding things that remind you of your financial situation or the foreclosure notices?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been deliberately avoiding things, other than I hate looking at the paperwork or dealing with calls about it. But I can’t say I’m staying away from certain places or people because of it.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself go through your daily routine?
No, I don’t think so. I feel overwhelmed and kind of on autopilot sometimes, but not like I’m outside my body watching myself.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or that you want to die?
No… I don’t think so. I’ve felt really stressed and worn down, but I haven’t been thinking that I want to die.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not much lately. I used to keep busy with church volunteering, fitness classes, and truck-club outings, but I’ve pretty much stopped showing up for all of that. Even at work, they took me out of the high-risk repair bay, so I’m not really doing the things I used to be involved in or feel good about.
